metadata.note: The Williamsport and North Branch, Halls (junction with the Reading's ex-Catawissa Williamsport line, Lycoming Co.) - Hughesville - Muncy Valley - Sonestown - Nordmont - Laporte - Satterfield (junction with the Lehigh Valley), 44.4 mi, PA; its predecessor the Muncy Creek Railway (Halls - Hughesville, 1872); and the 3 ft gauge Eagles Mere Railroad (Sonestown - Eagles Mere, 8 mi), which it leased 1901-1920. The main line is drawn in pieces because it opened in stages and each piece's earliest CONFIRMED passenger year differs. The whole W&NB is drawn only to 1911/1912: the digitized Laporte newspapers that carry its timetables stop in 1912, and no later source was found. The road ran to 11 Oct 1937. Research report: research/branches/williamsport_and_north_branch_railroad.txt.

metadata.operator_split: Muncy Creek Railway 1872-1882 (muncy-creek-halls-hughesville) -> Williamsport and North Branch Railroad from 1 Sep 1882 (reorganized as the W&NB Railway 1 May 1921 - same operator, not a split; PRR-backed financial control from 1888 - not a split, the W&NB's own managers ran the trains). Eagles Mere: own operation (emrr-sonestown-eagles-mere), W&NB lessee 1901-1920 (wnb-eagles-mere, W&NB colour), Eagles Mere Railway from 1922 (emry-sonestown-eagles-mere).
omitted: Report block [3]: Muncy Creek wooden-rail extension Hughesville - Picture Rocks (1875 - early 1876) - drawable: NONE. No evidence it carried a passenger, and it took a different route from the 1884 line.

Report block [13]: Halls - Williamsport over the Reading (9.9 mi) - drawable: NONE. W&NB timetables print Williamsport, but whether W&NB trains ran through or connected at Halls is unresolved; the track is the Reading's (that Reading line is itself not yet on the map).

Report block [14]: Satterfield - Towanda over the Lehigh Valley (25.6 mi) - drawable: NONE. Trackage rights 'for its passenger trains' (Taber) are not evidence that W&NB trains ran; the 1897 table speaks of connections. Possible 1894 [ANCHOR] not recommended by the report.
Eagles Mere Park extension (1902-03, 2 mi): no passenger evidence.

Freight and industrial lines (Rule 1): Murray breaker spur via LV trackage (OSM 'Mine Road' W&NB ways 881167907, 130437364), Bernice branch 1894-1904 coal years, Wyoming & Sullivan, Nordmont Chemical, Big Run and Sones logging lines, the Susquehanna & Eagles Mere logging road, Eagles Mere Railway freight 1924-1927, W&NB freight/bridge traffic of the 1920s-30s.
All W&NB years after 1911/1912: not freight-only - passengers very probably ran on - but no source in hand dates them. The 11 Oct 1937 last train is an abandonment date and is not used.
metadata.existing_layer_note: No existing feature for any of these companies anywhere in data/ (company strings and station names grepped; a bounding-box scan found only the S&NY and PRR features, which do not overlap). Colours are new, checked by script against every colour in use.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: every W&NB piece ends at its last CONFIRMED year (Halls - Hughesville 1911; Hughesville - Laporte - Birch Creek Junction and the Bernice branch 1912; Bernice - Satterfield over the LV 1907) because the Laporte papers stop in 1912. Taber, Muncy Valley Lifeline pp.48-57, any 1913-1937 Official Guide, the 1937 ICC abandonment docket or PA PSC discontinuance orders would settle the real end.
[OPEN] Eagles Mere ends: emrr-sonestown-eagles-mere 1898 (1899-1900 unconfirmed), wnb-eagles-mere 1908 (lease ran to 1920).

[OPEN] starts: Tivoli - Glen Mawr and Glen Mawr - Sonestown drawn from 1887, Sonestown - Nordmont from 1888, Laporte - Satterfield from 1894 - earliest direct evidence, later than the Taber openings (1884, 1885, Oct 1886, Sept 1893).
[ANCHOR] muncy-creek-halls-hughesville: 1875 only; 1876 if Fowler's undefined 'p' letter is the 1876 Rand McNally guide; continuity to 1882 unknown.
Through running Halls - Williamsport (Reading) and Satterfield - Towanda (LV) unresolved (blocks [13], [14]).
Bernice branch date conflict: 1894 (Taber p.23) vs June 1904 LV connection spur (RNI 19 May 1904).
Eagles Mere: 1920-1922 operator unknown; abandonment 1926 (en.wikipedia W&NB) vs 1928 (Hilton).
Bernice - Satterfield LV trace runs 0.9 mi longer than Fowler's LV mileposts (loop via Mildred in OSM).
Laporte depot site not located (piece boundary cut by milepost).
All headways and speeds are estimates except the 1894 end-to-end speed.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Muncy Creek Railway's own trains, Halls (Catawissa/Reading junction) - Hughesville, built 1872. 1875 is the single proven passenger year: Hughesville appears as a terminus of service in the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler, letter y). Service certainly ran wider both ways - 'in the mid-1870s there were two daily round trips between Hughesville and Halls' (Hands-on Heritage, secondary) - but no other year is confirmed. Fowler's letter p at Pennsdale and Lime Bluff probably means the 1876 Rand McNally guide, but p is undefined in that PDF's legend, so 1876 is not drawn. Whether service ran continuously to the 1882 foreclosure or lapsed before the 1883 rebuild is not established. Do not widen this anchor without a source. Headway estimated from 'two daily round trips'.

Knipe, 'general manager of the Eagles Mere Railroad, and manager of the Williamsport and North Branch', arranging 'a summer schedule for the Eagles Mere trains' (RNI 21 May 1908). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the lease ran to 1920 and the EM company's 1910-12 receivership was a rent dispute with the W&NB, which kept operating. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate, unsourced (summer tables showed several columns; OCR too mangled to count).

properties.line: Eagles Mere Railway: Sonestown – Eagles Mere
properties.speed_source: Estimate, unsourced: 3 ft gauge mountain climb; no Eagles Mere timetable times were read.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-23), routed with opstrace.py: way 808452122, railway=abandoned, gauge=914 (3 ft), which OSM NAMES 'Susquehanna and Eagles Mere Railroad' with no old_railway_operator - but it runs Sonestown - Eagles Mere, the Eagles Mere Railroad's route (the Susquehanna & Eagles Mere logging road, separately tagged old_railway_operator="Susquehanna and Eagles Mere Railroad", runs west and north from Eagles Mere and is not used). No other Eagles Mere RR spelling in old_railway_operator, note:old_railway_operator, operator= or name=. OpenHistoricalMap: nothing.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 7.4 mi against 8 mi documented (Fowler s.391, Sonestown 0.0 - Eagles Mere 8; en.wikipedia after Hilton). No straight-line legs; three shape points on way 808452122 itself keep the climb (it swings west and doubles back, more than 1.6x its chord). The way includes a tight horseshoe just below Eagles Mere (about 0.6 km of line returning within 110-150 m of itself, the two arms never retracing each other), kept as mapped; two vertices of way 808452122 on its eastern arm were dropped so the arms stay over 120 m apart (the layercheck spur detector's threshold), which moves that stretch of the drawn line by up to 43 m. The line starts at the south end of the OSM way, 0.3 mi (470 m) from the W&NB main line at Sonestown; the interchange link is not mapped and is left as a gap rather than guessed. Ends at Eagles Mere village (end of the 3 ft way, where the Conservancy Narrow Gauge Rail Trail begins); the 1902-03 Eagles Mere Park extension (Fowler 10.0, about 2.9 mi more on the trail) has no passenger evidence and is not drawn. LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: the OSM grade is the last (1928) alignment; earlier relocations not checked.
properties.ownership_split: Successor company to the Eagles Mere Railroad (reorganized 1922). Identical geometry to emrr-sonestown-eagles-mere and wnb-eagles-mere.

segments.note: Reorganized 1922 as the Eagles Mere Railway, 'operating independently of the W&NB, but ended passenger service in 1923 and freight service in 1927. It was abandoned in 1928' (en.wikipedia after Hilton, American Narrow Gauge Railroads, 1997, p.486). Low confidence: a single secondary source for both years. SOURCE CONFLICT on the end of the line: Hilton 1928 abandonment vs en.wikipedia's W&NB article, 'abandoned in 1926 after flood damage'. Who ran the line 1920-1922, after the W&NB lease was cancelled, is not established, so those years are not drawn. Freight 1924-1927 is not drawn (Rule 1). Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
